gaps.sentence: It was pouring with rain. ___, the open-air concert went ahead.
gaps.explanation: The concert happened despite the rain: Nevertheless is concessive.

gaps.sentence: He whispered ___ the children wouldn't hear.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + wouldn't' expresses intended (here negative) purpose.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.
'Due to personal reasons' is the standard collocation for giving a cause.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: ___ the weather improves, the crossing will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: Unless = if the weather doesn't improve — matching the cancellation.
